title: Real-time magnetic resonance imaging (RT-MRI) for evaluating changes in swallowing, reflux, and lung mechanics in children with spinal muscular atrophy or Duchenne muscular dystrophy before and after spinal correction surgery
summary:
We treat children and adolescents with spinal problems. These children and adolescents have a condition called either spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) or Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD). These children and adolescents undergo spinal surgery. During the operation, the spine is rotated, which also changes the position of the cervical spine and likely the esophagus as well. This can also affect swallowing. In addition, the esophagus may be altered in such a way that food flows back from the stomach into the esophagus (reflux). Breathing may also be affected. 
Using a state-of-the-art method we call real-time magnetic resonance imaging (RT-MRI), we now aim to determine to what extent swallowing, reflux, and breathing differ in affected children compared to healthy children, and whether spinal surgery causes any changes. The results could potentially lead to new therapies in the future.
conditions: Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA), Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy
Spinal muscular atrophy and related syndromes

interventions.name:
Observational study: 

Patients with spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) or Duchenne muscular dystrophy who are scheduled for long-segment dorsal spinal fusion surgery will undergo RT-MRI examinations at three time points (before surgery, 3–6 months afterward, and 12 months afterward) to assess swallowi

Healthy and age-matched participants will be examined at one time point using RT-MRI (swallowing process, possible reflux, and respiratory mechanics). Additionally, pulmonary function tests and a phoniatric-pediatric audiological evaluation are planned.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients between the ages of 10 and 18 with SMA or Duchenne muscular dystrophy who are scheduled for spinal surgery at UMG, who routinely present at our clinic, and whose parents consent to their child’s inclusion in the study. As comparison controls, healthy subjects of the same age and gender as the patients, whose parents consent to their child’s inclusion in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Children with a pacemaker
Children with a magnetic implant (e.g., the MAGEC spinal implant)
Children with intraocular or intraspinal metal fragments
Children with claustrophobia
Children with severe swallowing difficulties and a risk of aspiration
Children being treated at UMG for another medical condition.

Wearing braces is not a contraindication.
